display_title: Jio Platforms Launches Landmark Indian IPO
display_title_he: ג'יו פלטפורמס יוצאת להנפקה היסטורית בהודו
short_summary: Jio Platforms, the digital and telecommunications arm of Reliance Industries backed by Meta and Google, is seeking up to $3.2 billion in India's biggest domestic stock offering.

sources.name: CNBC
sources.title: Meta- and Google-backed Jio Platforms to raise up to $3.2 billion in historic IPO in India

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.title: Ambani’s Jio seeks to raise $3.2B in what could be India’s biggest IPO

paragraphs: Jio Platforms, the digital arm of Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s conglomerate Reliance Industries and India’s largest telecom operator, is preparing to launch a historic initial public offering. According to official stock exchange filings, the company intends to raise up to 302 billion rupees—approximately $3.2 billion—by offering 270 million shares priced between 1,065 and 1,119 rupees apiece. The public subscription period will commence on October 21 and conclude on October 23, preceded by bidding for anchor institutional investors on October 19.

In rupee terms, the transaction represents India's largest share sale in history, surpassing Hyundai Motor India’s 278.7 billion rupee listing in 2024, although it trails that same offering marginally in dollar terms, where the automaker raised $3.3 billion. At the upper ceiling of the price band, Jio Platforms would secure a market valuation of roughly 10.3 trillion rupees, or around $108.3 billion. While this valuation indicates considerable expansion compared to the roughly $65 billion valuation recorded when the company raised over $20 billion from international backers in 2020, it remains substantially lower than prior market projections. Notably, Indian market intelligence firm Prime Database had anticipated proceeds approaching 377 billion rupees.

The impending float also tests public appetite for a venture backed by prominent global technology firms. Reliance Industries retains an equity stake exceeding 66 percent, while Meta Platforms holds nearly 10 percent through its affiliate Jaadhu Holdings, and Google International possesses 7.7 percent. Meta, previously known as Facebook, had originally invested $5.7 billion, while Google committed $4.5 billion; IPO filings confirm that neither tech giant intends to sell existing shares. The company has allocated shares worth up to 25 billion rupees for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders, alongside 5 billion rupees earmarked for employees, who are entitled to a discount of 54 rupees per share.

Jio Platforms continues to market itself as an innovative digital technology ecosystem rather than a standard utility, but some analysts urge caution. Deven Choksey, managing director of Mumbai-based DRChoksey Finserv, observed that Jio remains fundamentally a telecommunications enterprise whose entertainment and gaming applications primarily stimulate data consumption, generating revenue mostly through connectivity sales. Operationally, the company remains lucrative: during the quarter ending in June, revenue rose nearly 12 percent year-on-year to 391.7 billion rupees, while net profit grew 9 percent to 77.6 billion rupees. Jio plans to allocate up to 275 billion rupees of the proceeds to eliminate debt at its primary subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm, reserving the balance for general corporate purposes.

Concurrently, competitive friction looms over satellite communications. Jio intends to deploy approximately 1,600 low Earth orbit satellites and 23 ground stations across India. This initiative has reignited a feud between Ambani and Elon Musk, who recently accused the Indian billionaire of obstructing Starlink’s domestic debut to perpetuate monopolistic exploitation. Musk’s criticism arrives more than a year after Jio and rival operator Airtel established agreements with SpaceX to distribute Starlink services, pending regulatory clearance. Indian authorities have dismissed Musk’s claims.
